title: 'Oye maar kaise raha hai': On cam, Delhi minister Parvesh Verma slaps man
content: Captured on video during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar, Delhi, PWD Minister Parvesh Verma's unexpected slap to a young man has stirred controversy. Released by the Aam Aadmi Party, the footage shows Verma confronting the individual before a security guard intervenes. This incident has ignited debate regarding the behavior of public servants in the line of duty, attracting the attention of numerous onlookers.

title: NEET leak fallout: CISF to guard NTA’s confidential exam areas
content: Responding to the alarming issue of exam paper leaks, the National Testing Agency has fortified its security protocols. A dedicated team of 29 CISF personnel is now assigned to the agency's new office for rigorous oversight. In addition to advancing cybersecurity measures, the NTA is revisiting its entire examination-cycle systems to thwart unauthorized access. Independent audits will also be conducted, aiming for a significant improvement in examination integrity moving forward.

title: Tamil Nadu govt rolls back law and order department’s RTI exemption amid backlash
content: The Tamil Nadu government faced backlash after it issued a notification that exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information (RTI) Act. Critics, including numerous political leaders, argued that such an action would jeopardize transparency and obstruct public access to crucial law records. In response to widespread criticism, the government promptly withdrew the exemption, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the RTI Act.

title: ‘Minister’s aides threatened to kill me’: Man recalls being slapped by Parvesh Verma
content: During a recent road inspection in Tilak Nagar, a controversial act unfolded as PWD Minister Parvesh Verma reportedly slapped a young man named Saheb, invited to report on road damages. Eyewitnesses reported that after Saheb raised concerns about the poor conditions, Verma's reaction escalated into violence, accompanied by associates who intimidated him.

title: New Green Card rules from September: Categories affected and those exempt
content: Beginning in September 2026, the USCIS unveiled new regulations affecting Green Card seekers. These guidelines emphasize the financial self-sufficiency of applicants while excluding those in humanitarian categories. Nearly all applicants, including family and various occupational groups, must satisfy these criteria. While the Form I-864, Affidavit of Support, is crucial, it cannot guarantee approval on its own.

title: Asian Games: Tejaswin Shankar wins decathlon bronze after 1500m triumph
content: In an impressive display of athleticism, Tejaswin Shankar clinched the decathlon bronze medal at the Asian Games by triumphing in the 1500m race. With a remarkable total of 7,934 points, he secured a podium position, while Japan's Yuma Maruyama took the gold. Meanwhile, Ancy Sojan finished just shy of gold in the women's long jump, placing second behind China's Yingying Huang.

title: New homes, new jobs: Why this Denver-area ZIP code is drawing movers
content: Aurora, Colorado's 80019 ZIP code is now the most popular destination for movers in the United States. The ranking is based on a significant number of new housing developments in the area. Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, remains in second place due to military relocations that dominate its movement figures. Florida has three spots in the top ten, appealing to retirees and remote workers.

title: Kashmera backs Sunita Ahuja: Actor questions Komal Rani’s affair claims
content: Kashmera Shah defended Sunita Ahuja after Komal Rani's cryptic Instagram note, calling it the first time women in their family were labelled "murderers" for protecting loved ones. Komal Rani questioned Sunita's intentions without naming her. The controversy follows affair rumours between Govinda and Komal Rani, his 'Roopa' co-star, since earlier this year.

title: Asian Games: Ancy Sojan misses gold by 2cm, Shaili loses bronze on final jump
content: In a nail-biting finish at the Asian Games 2026, Ancy Sojan just fell short of clinching the gold medal in the women's long jump, achieving a stellar jump of 6.53m, only to be bested by China's Yingying Huang at 6.55m. Shaili Singh, meanwhile, faced disappointment, slipping to fourth place with a last jump that pushed her down after Mengyi Tan's leap.

title: Florida used robot rabbits to hunt Burmese pythons threatening the Everglades
content: Florida is testing solar-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Developed by the South Florida Water Management District and University of Florida, the robotic decoys mimic prey using heat and scent while AI cameras detect approaching snakes. Officials can then alert trained removal agents, adding technology to Florida’s wider python control efforts.

title: 'Didn't collect ID': Guwahati homestay where student, ‘lover’ stayed 5 times sealed
content: Nimisha Thakuria's death has prompted police to seal Rudra’s Kitchen homestay at Dharapur. Investigators are examining guest documentation and prior visits made by her and Ashiq Ali. Police indicated that Ali's claim of suicide has not yet been confirmed. The circumstances surrounding Nimisha's unconscious state and subsequent death are being explored. Authorities are investigating all possible angles related to the case.

title: 'We trusted EC in 2017': Akhilesh alleges poll officials deleted SP votes in 2022
content: Akhilesh Yadav has accused the Election Commission of deliberately deleting votes belonging to the Samajwadi Party. He argues that this malpractice has been ongoing for years but is only now gaining attention. In his statement, he noted that voters from the 2019 elections were unjustly denied the opportunity to vote in 2022. This controversy follows recent revelations about objections within the Election Commission regarding the electoral rolls revision.

title: RAF Fairford alert: Several arrested, homes evacuated near US air base - key details
content: Several men were arrested near RAF Fairford on suspicion of violations under the Explosives Act. Residents of the nearby village of Whelford were evacuated to a leisure center in Cirencester. Police established a cordon around the area while an Army explosive ordnance disposal team assessed several vehicles. Counter-terrorism police are leading the investigation but have not confirmed a link to RAF Fairford.

title: New mobile recharge rules: 30-day plans, call-only options and more
content: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India has unveiled enhancements to prepaid mobile recharge options, featuring more voice-and-SMS-only Special Tariff Vouchers. Users can now access plans with a validity of 30 days or less. This initiative is especially beneficial for senior citizens and budget-conscious individuals who prefer voice-only prepaid plans without data, addressing concerns raised by Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha.

title: 'Marriage doesn't advance age': HC rejects Muslim personal law defence in POCSO case
content: The Delhi High Court has taken a firm stance by ruling against a man who married a 16-year-old under Muslim personal law, emphasizing that this does not exempt him from POCSO charges concerning sexual activity. While the girl asserted her consent, the court reiterated the importance of legal safeguards for minors. Attempts to contest the FIR based on her claims were rejected, underscoring the inviolability of child protection laws.

title: Asian Games: Harita Bhadra holds nerve in photo-finish to bag 200m bronze
content: In a thrilling finish, Harita Bhadra grabbed a bronze in the women’s 200m race, recording 23.20 seconds. Just 0.01 seconds later, Japan’s Abigeirufuka Ido crossed the line. Gold went to Indonesia's Shanti Pereira and silver to China's Yujie Chen. With nine athletics medals amassed at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, India’s team is set to pursue more victories as the competition continues to heat up.

title: UP double murder: Retired Army man, 1st wife found dead in pool of blood
content: In a tragic event, retired Army veteran Shamsuddin and his wife Saddo Begum were discovered murdered in their residence, the police alerted by neighbors. Their bodies were located amidst a pool of blood, prompting forensic experts and a dog squad to join the inquiry. With the motive still unknown, multiple investigation teams are being formed.

title: Sibal escalates SIR row, demands CEC’s removal and review of elections
content: Kapil Sibal has raised concerns over the Election Commission's decision-making under Gyanesh Kumar during a ten-month period. His allegations include that decisions were made unilaterally, bypassing other commissioners and statutory protocols. Sibal has called for an investigation into the electoral rolls and recent elections conducted in Bihar and West Bengal. In response, the Election Commission acknowledged concerns and proposed several corrective measures to address them.

title: Korea's KF-21 is flying, AMCA still on paper: The fighter-jet race India cannot afford to lose
content: As South Korea's KF-21 program progresses towards operational capability, India's AMCA program is still finalizing construction partners. The KF-21 has completed extensive testing and received certification, with production already underway. In contrast, India's bid process for an AMCA partner has faced multiple delays, slowing prototype development. The Indian Air Force currently operates below its authorized fighter strength, increasing operational challenges.

title: Heathrow expansion faces fresh hurdle as UK PM withholds third runway backing
content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has voiced significant concerns regarding the proposed third runway at Heathrow Airport. He pointed out the necessity of addressing the long-standing worries of local residents. The expansion's timeline could stretch by four years, with operations potentially starting in 2039. Heathrow's struggle with capacity issues sharply contrasts with other major European airports, fueling an ongoing debate centered on community impact and infrastructure demands.

title: Three matches in 24 hours! PV Sindhu criticises badminton schedule at Asian Games
content: PV Sindhu played twice on Saturday, with her third-round match finishing after midnight. She was back on court on Sunday afternoon for her quarterfinal against China's Chen Yufei, which she lost.

title: From warship to AIR 2: How IAF doctor cracked NEET PG 2026

She graduated from the Armed Forces Medical College with commendable academic records and personal dedication. Pallakshi balanced her military duties and rigorous studies to achieve this milestone. Supported by her family, she followed her dream of becoming a doctor against their engineering backgrounds.

title: 2.5% deposit, £600,000 price cap: How UK's new home-buying scheme will work
content: The UK government plans to launch a new scheme called 'Your First Home' to assist first-time buyers. This initiative allows qualifying individuals to acquire new-build properties with a minimal deposit of 2.5 percent. Eligible buyers will also receive a government equity loan for up to 20 percent of the property's value to ease financial burdens. The scheme is intended to stimulate demand for new housing and support the construction sector.

title: ‘UPI must remain zero MDR’: Mobile retailers announce October 2 protest
content: Mobile phone retailers across India are set to observe a 'No UPI Day' on October 2. This protest arises against the proposed 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions over Rs 2,000. The All India Mobile Retailers Association highlights additional costs that may impact small retailers significantly. The government insists consumers will not bear the MDR, which will apply starting October 15.

title: Market mood check: Crude, US-Iran talks and economic data to drive Dalal Street this week
content: This week on Dalal Street sees a shortened holiday schedule as geopolitical concerns and volatile oil prices loom large. Analysts believe negotiations between the US and Iran might sway both oil costs and the rupee's value. Investors are on high alert for shifts in global bond yields that impact emerging markets, while key domestic metrics like industrial production and auto sales are set to provide essential economic insights.

title: Asian Games: No squash gold for India as Anahat Singh, Abhay Singh win silver
content: Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh showcased their skills at the Asian Games, clinching silver medals for India. Anahat faced a tough match against Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam, while Abhay was outplayed by Ng Eain Yow. This was a significant achievement for Anahat, marking her as a finalist in women's singles. Additionally, the country bagged a bronze in mixed doubles, enhancing the overall medal count.

title: 'Gaza on verge of exploding': Egypt spy chief warned Israel before Oct 7
content: Egypt’s intelligence chief Abbas Kamel visited Israel on September 26, warning officials about impending Hamas aggression. He urged Israel to make economic concessions to prevent escalation, signaling a dangerous situation in Gaza. Despite his warnings, Israeli officials reportedly did not take specific action in response. Numerous warnings continued to emerge from Egypt and other nations leading up to the October 7 attack.
